6.4.2.1. Continuous static abilities generated from resolved effects affect all cards in play that the ability can affect. These static abilities last
for as long as their duration is active and are functional only during their existence. When the duration is over, the effect ceases to
exist, and all affected cards lose the effect immediately. If a card that would be affected by a continuous static ability generated from a
resolved effect is played after that ability has resolved, the card has that ability’s effect as it comes into play.
Example: Restoring Atlantis is an action with the effect, “Your characters can't be challenged until the start of your next turn.” When the
effect resolves, a continuous static effect is generated and continues to apply to all characters it could apply to until the duration ends. If
a character is played after the effect resolves, that character is also affected by this continuous static effect.
texto_2.3:
6.4.2.1. Continuous static abilities generated from resolved effects affect all cards in play, game rules, and game states that the ability can
affect. These static abilities last for as long as their duration is active and are functional only during their existence. When the duration
is over, the effect ceases to exist, and all cards in play, game rules, and game states are no longer affected. If a card that would be
affected by a continuous static ability generated from a resolved effect is played after that ability has resolved, the card has that
ability’s effect as it comes into play.
Example: Restoring Atlantis is an action with the effect, “Your characters can’t be challenged until the start of your next turn.” When the
effect resolves, a continuous static effect is generated and continues to apply to all characters it could apply to until the duration ends. If
a character is played after the effect resolves, that character is also affected by this continuous static effect.

for as long as the card generating them is in play. If a card generating a static ability leaves play, its effect ends as soon as the card is
removed from the Play zone, and all affected cards lose the effect immediately. If a card that would be affected by a continuous static
ability generated from a card in play is played after that ability has resolved, the card has that ability’s effect as it comes into play.
Example: A player has Weight Set and Grumpy – Bad-Tempered in play. Weight Set has an ability called Training that reads, “Whenever
you play a character with 4 {S} or more, you may pay 1 {I} to draw a card.” Grumpy has an ability called There's Trouble A-Brewin' that
reads, “Your other Seven Dwarfs characters get +1 {S}.” The player plays Happy – Good-Natured, which has 3 {S}. Happy comes into play
with the static ability from Grumpy applying to him and has a {S} value of 4. Because Happy is played with 4 {S}, the triggered ability on
Weight Set occurs.

6.4.2.3. A continuous static ability generated from a card that’s in play affects all cards in play, game rules, or game states the ability can affect.
These static abilities last for as long as the card generating them is in play. If a card generating a static ability leaves play, its effect
ends as soon as the card is removed from the Play zone, and all cards in play, game rules, or game states are no longer affected. If a
card is played that would be affected by a continuous static ability generated from a card already in play, the card is affected as it
comes into play.

reads, “Your other Seven Dwarfs characters get +1 {S}.” The player plays Happy – Good-Natured, which has 3 {S}. Happy comes into play
with the static ability from Grumpy applying to him and has a {S} value of 4. Because Happy is played with 4 {S}, the triggered ability on

6.7.6.1. If multiple players would act at the same time because of a resolving effect and that effect has multiple effects, the active player
performs their part of the first effect first, then all other players do so in turn order. After the first of the multiple effects is resolved,
the active player performs the next part of the effect, then all other players do so in turn order, repeating this process until each of the
multiple effects is fully resolved.
Example: Thomas O’Malley has an ability called Lucky Break that reads, “Whenever this character quests, each player reveals the top
card of their deck. Put the card with the highest cost revealed this way, or each card tied for highest cost, into its player’s hand. Put the
rest on the bottom of their players’ decks.” When the active player quests with Thomas O’Malley, they first reveal the top card of their
deck, a card with an ink cost of 6. Then the opponent reveals the top card of their deck, which has an ink cost of 5. The first effect of the
triggered ability has been performed by both players, so the active player now performs the second part of the effect. The active player
puts their revealed card into their hand because it had the highest cost of the revealed cards. Since the opponent revealed a card that
wasn’t the highest cost or tied for the highest, they put their revealed card on the bottom of their deck.
